title: FLOOD: A Flexible Invariant Learning Framework for Out-of-Distribution Generalization on Graphs

problem.claim: Graph neural networks may fail to generalize under out-of-distribution settings because the training and test distributions differ.

gap.claim: Previous invariant-learning solutions leave the graph encoder immutable after invariant learning, limiting flexible adaptation to the target distribution.

contributions.claim: FLOOD is a flexible invariant learning framework for out-of-distribution generalization on graphs that combines invariant learning with bootstrapped learning.
Its invariant learning component constructs multiple environments through graph data augmentation and learns invariant representations under risk extrapolation.
Its bootstrapped learning component uses self-supervised training with a graph encoder shared with the invariant learning component, allowing refinement on the test set.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on transductive and inductive node classification tasks.
The authors report that FLOOD consistently outperforms other graph out-of-distribution generalization methods and improves generalization ability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph neural networks are successful in many domains but are commonly developed under the in-distribution assumption.
Distribution shift between training and test data can impair graph neural network generalization in out-of-distribution settings.
Prior invariant-learning methods do not flexibly adapt the graph encoder to the target distribution.
FLOOD combines invariant learning over augmented environments with self-supervised bootstrapped learning using a shared encoder that can be refined on the test set.
The authors evaluate FLOOD on transductive and inductive node classification and report consistent improvements over other graph out-of-distribution generalization methods.
